overview.text: Joy of All Who Sorrow is a family of images portraying the Mother of God amid people in distress. The OCA’s October 24 account explains the composition and recounts the healing associated with the Moscow image in 1688.

blocks.text: Mary appears full length, surrounded by people who are hungry, unclothed, oppressed, or otherwise suffering. Angels attend them and direct attention toward her. The OCA notes variants with Christ in her arms and variants without the Child, as well as differences in her garments.

blocks.text: The Moscow account concerns Euphemia, the sister of Patriarch Joachim, who suffered from a severe wound. In the narrative, a voice directs her to an image in the Transfiguration church on Ordynka. After the icon is brought and a service held, her healing on October 24, 1688 becomes the occasion for its feast. The same entry distinguishes the later Petersburg image associated with coins, rather than treating every image bearing this title as one physical object.

blocks.text: The OCA interprets the title as consolation in suffering and describes the Theotokos as interceding for those in need. Its explanation links the surrounding figures to the subject of the icon and to the care offered to the suffering.
